setup: Use the literal F, P_F, Q_i and tau from the frozen block report. Let x_i=i^2/tau, t_i=log(x_i), G_i(x)=x^(-1/2)Q_i(x), and e_i(x)=x^(-1/2)sum_(a<=i)mu(a)F(a/x). Here e_i is the normalized SHORT prefix; E_i^raw in the parent is unnormalized. The exact complete prime field is P(log x)=2e_i(x)-G_i(x) on x_i<=x<x_(i+1). Values and all derivative jets match at each seam, as proved in the parent B5a. All derivatives below are ordinary x derivatives with i fixed.
one_cell:
For every integer i>=2, define d_i=2sqrt(tau)mu(i)F(tau/i)/i. The exact value-jump law gives
 G_i(x_i)-G_(i-1)(x_(i-1))
 =d_i+integral_[x_(i-1),x_i] G_(i-1)-prime(x)dx.
Likewise
 e_i(x_i)-e_(i-1)(x_(i-1))
 =d_i/2+integral_[x_(i-1),x_i] e_(i-1)-prime(x)dx.
The upper-end derivatives refer to the smooth fixed-cutoff branch, not the derivative of a floor function. Subtracting these two laws in 2e-G cancels the seam term exactly, leaving the integral of the complete physical prime derivative. No interior integral has been set to zero.
seam_series:
For each fixed A>0 the actual rapid integer drive gives a fixed C_A with |F(r)|<=C_A r^A for0<r<=tau/2. Therefore
 |d_i|<=2C_A tau^(A+1/2) i^(-A-1), i>=2.
The series D_infinity=sum_(i>=2)d_i converges ABSOLUTELY, and
 |D_infinity-sum_(i=2)^N d_i|
 <=[2C_A tau^(A+1/2)/A]N^(-A).
All rate constants are chosen before N. This uses source flatness through the actual drive and does not assert global C-infinity regularity of F at0. No sign or zero value of D_infinity is inferred.
initial_value_and_global_drift:
Because F(tau)=0 and P_F(1/tau)=0, G_1(x_1)=e_1(x_1)=P(t_1)=0. Consequently the exact finite relations are
 G_N(x_N)=sum_(i=2)^N d_i+sum_(i=2)^N integral_[x_(i-1),x_i]G_(i-1)-prime,
 2e_N(x_N)=sum_(i=2)^N d_i+2sum_(i=2)^N integral_[x_(i-1),x_i]e_(i-1)-prime,
 P(t_N)=2sum_(i=2)^N integral e_(i-1)-prime-sum_(i=2)^N integral G_(i-1)-prime.
The committed short-prefix rapid theorem gives e_N(x_N)=O_A(N^-A), after rescaling its exponent in t_N=2logN-logtau. Thus the short-prefix INTERIOR series converges to -D_infinity/2, by this exact telescope; no separate claim of absolute convergence of that interior series is needed. The complete remaining drift is
 P(t_N)=-sum_(i=2)^N integral_[x_(i-1),x_i]G_(i-1)-prime(x)dx
          -D_infinity+O_A(N^-A).
This answers whether the E terms cancel: they cancel the seam contribution in the exact P step and aggregate to a fixed finite constant plus a rapid error. They do not eliminate the signed G interior drift.
rank_one_and_normalization_cost:
Let ell_Y=sum_(a<=Y)mu(a)/a, I=actualFlatSamplingMass>0, and R_Y(x)=sum_(a,b<=Y)mu(a)mu(b)R_F(x/(ab)), including the diagonal. Then Q_Y(x)=I*x*ell_Y^2+R_Y(x), and
 G_Y-prime(x)=(I/2)x^(-1/2)ell_Y^2
                 +x^(-1/2)R_Y-prime(x)-(1/2)x^(-3/2)R_Y(x).
The last normalization term cannot be omitted. Since sqrt(x_i)-sqrt(x_(i-1))=1/sqrt(tau), the positive rank-one part on the i-th native cell integrates EXACTLY to
 (I/sqrt(tau))*ell_(i-1)^2.
Thus the remaining complete drift has a nonnegative actual rank-one contribution (I/sqrt(tau))sum_(j=1)^(N-1)ell_j^2 and the full signed alias-derivative and alias-normalization integrals. No bound on that signed remainder or on the harmonic Mobius squares is supplied. Tiny or all-jet-flat seams do not control this bulk.
